chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah, Exalted is He, support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
“There is no harm in performing wudu (ablution) with used water.”

And he said: “Water with which a garment is washed, or with which a man performs ghusl from janabah, it is not permissible to perform wudu from it and the like of it. But as for the water with which a man performs wudu, so he washes his face and his hand with it into a clean thing, then there is no harm in another taking it and performing wudu with it.”

And indicating the permissibility of wudu with water used in minor ritual purity, in addition to this report, is the verse, and that the name of water applies to it without qualification. Use does not remove it from the unrestricted application of the name of water to it, so it must be that performing wudu with it is allowed unless something diverts from that; and there is nothing in the shari'ah that prevents its use, and this also indicates it.

key_terms.الشَّرِيعَةِ: the revealed law governing permissibility and prohibition
key_terms.الطَّهَارَةِ الصُّغْرَى: minor ritual purity as opposed to major ritual purification
key_terms.الْآيَةُ: the Quranic verse cited as supporting evidence
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْمُسْتَعْمَلِ: used water previously employed in purification

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform wudu with water that has already been used for wudu?
ai.summary: This text states that water previously used for wudu (ablution) remains permissible for performing wudu again, while water used for washing clothes or for ghusl from janabah is not to be used for wudu. It also argues that such used water still retains the name of water in an unrestricted sense, and nothing in the shari'ah prevents its use for minor ritual purification.
